q: Under Sec. 20 (Penalty Clause and Sanction), an unqualified individual, partnership, firm, corporation, or consortium that engages in architectural services in violation of R.A. 9266 and its IRR is subject to:
o: A written warning only, with no further legal consequence
Automatic revocation of any existing PRC license held by the offending party
Mandatory registration as an Architectural Firm within 90 days
Sanction/s by the appropriate public or private entities, without prejudice to filing criminal, civil, or other administrative cases under existing laws
n: Sec. 20 provides that unqualified persons/entities engaging in architectural services under R.A. 9266 and its IRR are subject to sanction/s by appropriate public or private entities, without prejudice to filing criminal, civil, or other administrative cases pursuant to existing laws. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 20)

q: Under Sec. 17 (Government Taxes on Professional Fees/Services), the Architect's fee under the Methods of Compensation and Schedule of Fees is described as:
o: Gross, inclusive of all taxes payable by the Owner
Subject to a fixed 12% withholding to be remitted directly by the Client to the BIR
Net to the Architect, with taxes such as VAT (other than income tax) imposed on the Architect as a result of the Project to be paid by the Owner
Net to the Owner, with the Architect shouldering all VAT and income tax
n: Sec. 17 states the Architect's fee is net to the Architect; any tax (exclusive of income tax), such as VAT, that government imposes on the Architect due to Project services shall be paid by the Owner. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 17)

q: R.A. No. 9266, cited as the basis for Sec. 20's penalty clause and sanctions, is also known as:
o: The Building Code of the Philippines
The Engineering Act of 2004
The Architecture Act of 2004
The Real Estate Service Act
n: R.A. No. 9266 is the Architecture Act of 2004, cited in both Sec. 15 and Sec. 20 as governing qualification to render architectural services. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 20; R.A. 9266)

q: Per the review deck's cross-reference on Sec. 22 (Effectivity), the Document's approval by the UAP National Board of Directors and the PRC/PRBoA recommendation took effect on what date?
o: October 15, 2014
July 4, 2013
January 1, 2015
September 19, 2016
n: The review deck notes that the effectivity of this Document (under the PRBoA Resolution on SPP Documents) took place on October 15, 2014. (Source: Methods of Compensation review notes, Slide 115 (Effectivity); cf. Architect's Guidelines, Sec. 22)

q: Under Sec. 18.3, the legal liabilities of the Architect shall be based on:
o: The Local Government Code
The Labor Code of the Philippines
The Civil Code of the Philippines
The Revised Penal Code
n: Sec. 18.3 provides that the legal liabilities of the Architect shall be based on the Civil Code of the Philippines. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 18.3)

q: Per the Definition of Terms, an 'Architectural Firm (AF)' is best described as:
o: A juridical person duly registered with the DTI (as a sole proprietorship) or with the SEC and PRC (as a professional partnership or architectural corporation) for group architectural practice by RLAs
A natural person holding a valid PRC license
Any construction company that hires architects as consultants
A government agency overseeing architectural practice
n: The Annexes define Architectural Firm (AF) as a juridical person registered with the DTI (sole proprietorship for individual practice) or with the SEC and PRC (professional partnership or architectural corporation for group practice by RLAs), subject to compliance with Sec. 37 of R.A. 9266 and its derivative regulations; 'Architect' and 'AF' may be used interchangeably. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Annexes A - Definition of Terms ('Architectural Firm'))

q: Within how many days from receipt of billing must the Client pay the Architect's fees, charges, and reimbursements before interest under Sec. 16 begins to accrue?
o: 45 calendar days
15 calendar days
60 calendar days
30 calendar days
n: Sec. 16 provides that interest applies to fees, charges and reimbursements 'due and not paid within thirty (30) days from receipt of billing.' (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 16)

q: Under Sec. 22, the Document becomes effective upon which combination of approvals?
o: Approval of the UAP National Board of Directors alone, without any other recommendation needed
A plebiscite among all registered and licensed architects nationwide
Publication in the Official Gazette alone, independent of UAP or PRBoA action
Approval of the UAP National Board of Directors and the recommendation of the PRC-PRBoA, implemented as part of a PRBoA-issued Resolution on SPP Documents
n: Sec. 22 states the Document 'shall be effective after approval of the [UAP] National Board of Directors and upon the recommendation of the PRC-PRBoA for implementation as part of the PRBoA-issued Resolution on the Standards of Professional Practice (SPP) Documents.' (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 22)

q: Under Sec. 21 (Amendments to this Document), who is tasked with preparing amendments to the Architect's Guidelines?
o: The PRC-PRBoA acting alone
The Supreme Court en banc

A Special Committee on the Standards of Professional Practice of the integrated and accredited professional organization of architects (IAPOA), in consultation with the PRC-PRBoA and other associations of architects
Any individual licensed architect who submits a written proposal
n: Sec. 21 provides that amendments shall be prepared by a Special Committee on the Standards of Professional Practice of the IAPOA, in consultation with the PRC-PRBoA and other associations of architects. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 21)

q: Under Sec. 16 (Interest Due on Late Payment of Fees), what rate of interest is the Architect entitled to on fees, other charges, and reimbursements that remain unpaid beyond the grace period?
o: A fixed 12% per annum regardless of market conditions
1% per month as fixed by the UAP National Board
The prevailing rate set by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP), mutually agreed upon by the Architect and Client
The legal interest rate under the Civil Code only, with no room for agreement between the parties
n: Sec. 16 entitles the Architect to interest at the prevailing rate set by the BSP, as mutually agreed upon by the Architect and the Client. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 16)

q: In the same scenario, what would the Client owe in TOTAL (principal + interest) at the time of payment on day 90?
n: Total due = principal (Php 1,000,000.00) + interest for the 60 overdue days (Php 10,000.00, per Sec. 16 computation) = Php 1,010,000.00. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 16 (illustrative computation))
scenario: An Architect billed a Client Php 1,000,000.00 in professional fees on March 1. The Client and Architect had mutually agreed, per Sec. 16, on an interest rate of 6% per annum (a rate within the range the BSP has set as a prevailing legal/monetary interest benchmark) to apply on any balance not paid within the 30-day grace period. The Client actually paid the full Php 1,000,000.00 exactly 90 days after billing (i.e., 60 days beyond the 30-day grace period).

q: Sec. 21 states that the UAP-IAPOA shall continuously enhance the contents of the Document. What is the stated purpose of this continuous enhancement?
o: To be responsive to new challenges and requirements of professional practice
To align with international building codes exclusively
To increase UAP membership dues
To reduce the number of SPP documents in circulation
n: Sec. 21 states the UAP-IAPOA shall continuously enhance the Document's contents 'to be responsive to new challenges and requirements of professional practice.' (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 21)

q: Aside from R.A. 9285, Sec. 19.1 also cites which issuance as governing Construction (and Consulting) Industry Arbitration?
o: E.O. No. 292
D.O. No. 174
A.O. No. 25
n: Sec. 19.1 cites E.O. No. 1000 as governing Construction (and Consulting) Industry Arbitration, alongside R.A. 9285 and the New Civil Code. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 19.1)

q: Sec. 15's prohibition on unlicensed/unregistered persons collecting architectural fees is grounded in which law?
n: Sec. 15 expressly cites R.A. 9266 (The Architecture Act of 2004) as the basis for the prohibition against unlicensed/unregistered persons collecting architectural fees. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 15)

q: Using the scenario above and simple annual interest, how much interest is owed for the 60 days the payment was overdue beyond the Sec. 16 grace period (use a 360-day year for simplicity)?
n: Interest = Principal x rate x time = Php 1,000,000 x 6% x (60/360) = Php 1,000,000 x 0.06 x 0.1667 = Php 10,000.00. This applies Sec. 16's rule that interest accrues on fees not paid within 30 days of billing, at the rate mutually agreed upon by the parties (here, illustratively set at 6% per annum, consistent with BSP-referenced rates). (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 16 (illustrative computation; specific rate is Architect-Client agreed, referencing prevailing BSP rate))
scenario: An Architect billed a Client Php 1,000,000.00 in professional fees on March 1. The Client and Architect had mutually agreed, per Sec. 16, on an interest rate of 6% per annum (a rate within the range the BSP has set as a prevailing legal/monetary interest benchmark) to apply on any balance not paid within the 30-day grace period. The Client actually paid the full Php 1,000,000.00 exactly 90 days after billing (i.e., 60 days beyond the 30-day grace period).

q: Under Sec. 22 (Effectivity), the Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances: Methods of Compensation & Schedule of Fees is designated as which UAP-IAPOA document number?
o: UAP-IAPOA Doc. 209
UAP-IAPOA Doc. 202
UAP-IAPOA Doc. 301
UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210
n: Sec. 22 identifies the document as 'UAP-IAPOA Doc. 210' — the Architect's Guidelines on Standards of Professional Practice (SPP) Compliances: Methods of Compensation & Schedule of Fees. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 22)

q: If the initial 14-day negotiation period under Sec. 19.2 fails, the parties may engage in mediation/conciliatory discussions with a neutral third party for how many additional calendar days, or immediately seek arbitration under the CIAC?
o: Another 30 calendar days
Another 60 calendar days
Another 7 calendar days
Another 14 calendar days
n: Sec. 19.2 allows another 14 calendar days for mediation/conciliatory discussions with a neutral third party, or the parties may immediately seek arbitration modes of ADR under the CIAC. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 19.2)

q: Which tax is explicitly EXCLUDED from the taxes that the Owner must shoulder on behalf of the Architect under Sec. 17?
o: National government taxes generally
Income tax
Value-Added Tax (VAT)
Local government taxes on professional services
n: Sec. 17 specifies that the tax the Owner pays is 'exclusive of income tax' — the Architect's own income tax remains the Architect's personal liability, while VAT and similar taxes arising from the Project are for the Owner's account. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 17)

q: Two parties to a Service Agreement are in a dispute over professional fees and cannot settle informally. Which of the following correctly summarizes the applicable dispute-resolution process under Sec. 19?
o: The dispute is resolved by the UAP National Board of Directors, with no court involvement
The dispute is automatically dismissed unless filed with the PRC-PRBoA within 30 days

The parties first negotiate for 14 days, then may mediate for another 14 days or go straight to CIAC arbitration under R.A. 9285/E.O. 1000, with a 6-month resolution guarantee and possible appeal to the Court of Appeals
The dispute must go directly to the Supreme Court for final resolution
n: Sec. 19.1-19.2 lay out a sequential ADR process: 14-day negotiation, then 14-day mediation/conciliation or immediate CIAC arbitration (governed by R.A. 9285 and E.O. 1000), with CIAC guaranteeing resolution within 6 months and the losing party able to appeal to the Court of Appeals. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 19.1-19.2)

q: Under Sec. 15 (Collection of Professional Fees) of the Architect's Guidelines, who is prohibited from collecting a fee for architectural services?
o: Any unlicensed and unregistered person
Any architect who has not secured professional liability insurance
Any architect who has not paid annual dues to the UAP
Any architect practicing outside Metro Manila
n: Sec. 15 states it is unlawful for any unlicensed and unregistered person to collect a fee for architectural services, as provided under R.A. 9266. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 15)

q: A Client received the Architect's billing but has not paid after 60 days. Under Sec. 16, what is the Architect entitled to on the overdue amount?
o: Automatic doubling of the professional fee as a penalty
Interest at the prevailing BSP rate, as mutually agreed upon, since the payment is already 30 days beyond the billing receipt date
Nothing, since the Methods of Compensation document does not cover late payment
Immediate termination of the Service Agreement with no further recourse
n: Since 60 days have passed (more than the 30-day grace period under Sec. 16), the amount is already due and not paid within 30 days, entitling the Architect to interest at the prevailing BSP rate as mutually agreed with the Client. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 16)

q: Per the Definition of Terms in the Annexes accompanying these Guidelines, the term 'Architect' refers only to:
o: Any employee of an Architectural Firm regardless of license status
A juridical person registered with the SEC
Any person who has completed an architecture degree, licensed or not
A Registered and Licensed Architect (RLA) — a natural person with a valid certificate of registration and valid professional identification card for the lawful practice of Architecture
n: The Annexes define 'Architect' as referring only to a Registered and Licensed Architect (RLA), a natural person with a valid certificate of registration and valid professional ID card (renewable 3-year license) for the lawful practice of Architecture; the term also covers Architect-of-Record, Architect-in-Charge of Construction, and Consulting Architect under R.A. 9266. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Annexes A - Definition of Terms ('Architect'))

q: Under Sec. 19.3, the exclusive venue for ADR proceedings involving Architect-Client disputes is the CIAC Office located at the corner of which two avenues in Makati City?
o: Sen. Gil Puyat Ave. and Makati Ave.
EDSA and Buendia Ave.
Ayala Ave. and Paseo de Roxas
Chino Roces Ave. and Kalayaan Ave.
n: Sec. 19.3 designates the exclusive venue of ADR proceedings as the CIAC Office at the corner of Sen. Gil Puyat Ave. and Makati Ave., Makati City. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 19.3)

q: An unlicensed individual, without registration, offers and performs architectural design services for a fee. Aside from possible sanctions under Sec. 20/R.A. 9266, what does Sec. 20 clarify about other legal remedies available?
o: Sanctions are imposed 'without prejudice' to filing appropriate criminal, civil, or other administrative cases under existing laws
The Client automatically forfeits the right to any refund
Only civil cases may be filed, criminal liability is barred
No other case may be filed once administrative sanctions are imposed
n: Sec. 20 explicitly states that sanctions are imposed 'without prejudice to the filing of appropriate criminal, civil or other administrative or cases pursuant to existing laws' — i.e., other remedies remain available in addition to sanctions. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 20)

q: After being prepared and subjected to consultation under Sec. 21, amendments to the Architect's Guidelines are submitted to which body for approval?
o: The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC)
The UAP National Board
The Department of Trade and Industry (DTI)
The Office of the President
n: Sec. 21 states that after preparation and consultation, amendments 'shall be then submitted to the UAP National Board for approval.' (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 21)

q: Under Sec. 19.2, once a dispute concerning the Service Agreement arises, how many calendar days do the Parties have for an initial negotiation period before either may proceed to mediation/conciliation?
o: 30 calendar days
14 calendar days
7 calendar days
21 calendar days
n: Sec. 19.2 gives the Parties a negotiation period of fourteen (14) calendar days; failure to resolve authorizes either party to pursue mediation/conciliatory discussions. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 19.2)

q: Under Sec. 18.2, an Architect may secure professional liability insurance, malpractice insurance, or an equivalent bond commensurate with the project's nature and the Architect's compensation. How is the cost of this insurance/bond treated?
o: It is deducted from the Architect's professional fee as a mandatory withholding
It forms part of the total project cost chargeable to the Client
It is a personal expense the Architect may never pass on
It is shouldered equally by the Architect and the PRC-PRBoA
n: Sec. 18.2 states that the cost of securing professional liability/malpractice insurance or its equivalent bond 'shall form part of the total project cost chargeable to the Client.' (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 18.2)

q: Under Sec. 19.1 (Arbitration), a dispute between the Architect and the Client regarding services under the Service Agreement shall be settled in accordance with which law?
o: R.A. 9266, the Architecture Act of 2004
R.A. 9184, the Government Procurement Reform Act
Batas Pambansa Blg. 344
R.A. 9285, the Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Act of 2004
n: Sec. 19.1 provides that disputes shall be settled in accordance with R.A. No. 9285, the Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) Act of 2004, and E.O. No. 1000 governing Construction (and Consulting) Industry Arbitration, as well as applicable provisions of the New Civil Code. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 19.1)

q: Under Sec. 18.1 (Professional and Civil Responsibility), the Architect is legally and professionally responsible before the State and civilly liable for:
o: The architectural design part of the project, and the conduct and performance of services to clients whether in government, private sector, or civil society
Only the structural engineering aspects of the project
Only projects funded by government agencies
The Owner's compliance with local zoning ordinances
n: Sec. 18.1 provides that the Architect is legally and professionally responsible before the State and civilly liable on the architectural design part of the project, and responsible for the conduct and performance of services to clients across government, private sector, or civil society. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 18.1)

q: Sections 15 to 22 of the Architect's Guidelines are best described as:
o: Fee schedules specific to each project classification
A separate schedule of payments unrelated to the Methods of Compensation

General/administrative and legal provisions that apply across the whole Methods of Compensation document, covering fee collection, interest, taxes, liability, dispute resolution, penalties, amendments, and effectivity
Definitions of architectural project classifications (Groups 1-10)
n: Sec. 15-22 form the closing 'General Provisions' (Rule 4) of the Methods of Compensation document, covering cross-cutting administrative and legal matters that apply to the whole document rather than a specific fee-computation method. (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 15-22 (General Provisions))

q: Under Sec. 19.2, the Construction Industry Arbitration Commission (CIAC), which also handles disputes concerning professional or consulting services, guarantees resolution of the issues presented within what period, after which the losing party may file a Petition for Review before the Court of Appeals?
o: Three (3) months
One (1) year
Six (6) months
Two (2) years
n: Sec. 19.2 guarantees a resolution of the issues presented within a six (6) month period under CIAC, after which the losing party may file a Petition for Review before the Court of Appeals (CA). (Source: Architect's Guidelines on SPP Compliances, Sec. 19.2)
